Backend: grep core/ providers/ server.py for CloudFormation (stacks, change sets, templates); if no engine exists, add a self-contained core with conformance tests that creates/updates/deletes stacks by provisioning the template's resources through the existing cores, and render anything it can't model as NotSimulated
List / create / detail / edit / delete round-trips through the native API the SDK and CLI use

core/capabilities/aws/cloudformation.json: one entry per console section, ids start with 'aws.cloudformation.'; tests/conformance/test_capabilities.py must pass
Keep consoles/src/aws/kit/Capability.jsx as on base (add your JSON import), list the service ONCE in registry.js

Register any NEW core in wasm/build_cores.py + wasm/nano-boot.js (own line, never inside a // comment) + core/nano_registry.py + core/nano_persist.py — tests/conformance/test_nano_core_manifest.py checks this
Use unique variable names in consoles/tests/smoke-aws.mjs (other blocks already use R, RDB, ROLE, …); write 'Vyomi' as plain text; commit your source
note:
DEPTH PASS (the base console is merged). Goal: turn this service's sub-sections and config sections into REAL backend integrations. For EACH capability entry listed in `depth_targets` decide:
  BUILD — Vyomi can model it in the shared core (state + native API semantics): implement it in core/<svc>_core.py (and the offline route if offline lacks it), add conformance checks in tests/conformance/, raise the entry's level in core/capabilities/<cloud>/<svc>.json (not_simulated→limited/full, config_only→limited/full where now ENFORCED, limited→full where a limitation is removed), wire the console section to it with a UI↔native-API round trip in consoles/tests/smoke-<cloud>.mjs and a "live" fixture for any list/detail page.
  KEEP HONEST — only if it needs something a local simulator cannot run (a separate product, real hardware/network, billing, third-party identity): leave it NotSimulated and put the concrete reason in the entry's `limitations`.
Prefer behaviour that is ENFORCED (e.g. lifecycle rules actually expire objects, a DLQ really receives, a policy really denies) over config that is only stored. Real coverage must go UP; nothing may regress: fidelity ≥ 90%, every capability claim true on nano AND offline, smokes green. Do not edit consoles/honest-allowlist.json or .github/.
House rules: keep consoles/src/<cloud>/kit/Capability.jsx as on base (add JSON imports only), list the service ONCE in registry.js, register any NEW core in wasm/build_cores.py + wasm/nano-boot.js (own line, never inside a // comment) + core/nano_registry.py + core/nano_persist.py (tests/conformance/test_nano_core_manifest.py), unique variable names in the smoke files, 'Vyomi' as plain text, re-vendor with python3 wasm/build_cores.py, rebuild bundles, COMMIT your source.

depth_targets.title: Template resources provisioned through the real S3 / DynamoDB / SNS / SQS / IAM engines
limitations: Only AWS::S3::Bucket, AWS::DynamoDB::Table, AWS::SNS::Topic, AWS::SQS::Queue, AWS::IAM::Role and the no-infrastructure AWS::CloudFormation::WaitCondition[Handle] are provisioned.
A template with any other resource type fails CreateStack/UpdateStack honestly (rolled back, never a silent success) — the same way a real account without the matching service permissions would fail.

depth_targets.title: Template body, JSON and a YAML subset (short-form !Ref/!GetAtt/!Sub/!Join/!If/…, long-form Fn:: mappings), intrinsic function resolution
limitations: The YAML parser covers block mappings/sequences and single-line short-form tags; multi-line short-form tag arguments are not supported (use the JSON or long-form Fn:: syntax instead).

depth_targets.title: Drift detection
limitations: Drift is detected by checking whether each resource still exists in its owning service's store — a resource deleted independently (e.g. through the S3 console) shows as DELETED. Property-level drift (a resource edited, not deleted, outside the stack) is not detected.

depth_targets.title: StackSets (create, describe, list, delete)
limitations: Control plane only — a StackSet's own template/parameters are stored, but Vyomi does not deploy stack instances across accounts or Regions (ListStackInstances always returns empty).

depth_targets.title: Stack refactors
limitations: A refactor moves a resource's runtime state (ref, physical id, properties) between two EXISTING stacks — it does not create new stacks from StackDefinitions, the way the real ListStackRefactorActions / template-diff flow does.

depth_targets.title: Public extensions registry and publisher registration
limitations: The third-party extension marketplace and publisher workflow are out of Vyomi's scope.

depth_targets.title: Hooks (overview, invocation summary, hooks list)
limitations: CloudFormation Hooks are out of Vyomi's scope.

depth_targets.title: IaC generator (scan an account's existing resources into a template)
limitations: Scanning existing account resources into a generated template is out of Vyomi's scope.

depth_targets.title: Template studio editor (YAML/JSON, Validate)
limitations: The template + text editing and Validate action are real; the visual resource Canvas view is not simulated.

depth_targets.title: CloudFormation Spotlight (editorial content)
limitations: Spotlight is an editorial content feed, not an API surface — out of Vyomi's scope.
